name: 185. Routing retries, first-token cutoffs and refused keys against the provider error fixture (routing-error-fixture)
description:
Routing rows that need an upstream to fail on demand: a 500 retried three times, a slow first token, a caller key the upstream refuses. Real providers cannot fail on cue, so each row's providers are run-scoped OpenAI-backed custom providers whose base URL is the provider error fixture (tests/e2e/api/runners/provider-error-fixture.mjs), and each key serves the run's model as an alias of a fixture model tagged with the run and the key (upstream-500~<run>-a1), so the fixture's hit counts (GET /__hits) are the row's own attempts per key. The rows need the management API, governance and the logs, and rows 3 and 8 also a provider on OpenAI with the gateway's OpenAI key, so they run against an ordinary gateway (the python integration profile works) with the fixture started next to it: run with providerErrorFixture=1, and providerErrorFixtureUrl when the fixture is not on http://127.0.0.1:8791. Every row is skipped otherwise. Row 8 also needs the runner's openaiKey.

Rows: (1) a virtual key's weight-1 primary answering 500 is tried three times before its weight-0 fallback serves, and the session's next turn starts on the fallback with no attempt on the primary; (2) the same with the model catalog's pick; (3) a rule target answering 500 is tried three times, a fallback whose provider budget is spent is refused by governance without an upstream call, and the next fallback serves on one attempt; (4) max_retries lowered from 2 to 0 through the provider API applies from the next request: three attempts, then one; (5) a rule fallback pinned to a deleted key is skipped without an upstream call after the target's three 500s, and the next fallback, another provider, serves on its key, streamed and not; (6) a streaming target that holds its first token for two seconds is cut at its 500ms deadline, its attempt recorded as a timeout with ttft_timeout, and the fallback serves, while a non-streaming request and a stream with no fallback wait for it; (7) a session bound to the fallback's pinned key whose two pinned keys then both answer 500 returns the fallback's error with its headers after three attempts on each pin, and once both heal the next turn follows the rule; (8) a caller's direct key on a bare model goes to whichever provider the virtual key picks, so requests that start on the provider refusing it are served by the other on its own keys, and the refusing provider's own key is never used; (9) on streamed chat, Responses, /openai and /anthropic, a virtual key's primary answering 500 is tried three times before the weight-0 fallback serves turn 1, and turn 2 starts on the fallback with no attempt on the primary; (10) a streamed request whose rule-pinned target answers 500 before its first chunk is served to [DONE] by the fallback's pinned key, the session's next stream starts there, and a target that sends its first chunk and then drops the connection gets no fallback; (11) a provider that does not answer within its one-second request timeout is cut there, its attempt recorded as a timeout with 504 and request_timed_out, and the fallback serves. Each row deletes what it made. Run with FEATURE="routing-error-fixture".
